crossrefs.text: A manʼs pride will bring him low, but a humble spirit will obtain honor.
You shall not have two differing weights in your bag, one heavy and one light.
For everyone who behaves dishonestly in regard to these things is detestable to the LORD your God.
The fear of the LORD is the instruction of wisdom, and humility comes before honor.
Honest scales and balances are from the LORD; all the weights in the bag are His concern.
Ill-gotten treasures profit nothing, but righteousness brings deliverance from death.
Pride goes before destruction, and a haughty spirit before a fall.
It is better to be lowly in spirit among the humble than to divide the spoil with the proud.
Only with sound guidance should you wage war, and victory lies in a multitude of counselors.
Plans fail for lack of counsel, but with many advisers they succeed.
Set plans by consultation, and wage war under sound guidance.
He who reveals secrets is a constant gossip; avoid the one who babbles with his lips.
You must not go about spreading slander among your people. You must not endanger the life of your neighbor. I am the LORD.
When words are many, sin is unavoidable, but he who restrains his lips is wise.
Righteousness exalts a nation, but sin is a disgrace to any people.
Argue your case with your neighbor without betraying anotherʼs confidence,
Hallelujah! Blessed is the man who fears the LORD, who greatly delights in His commandments.
His descendants will be mighty in the land; the generation of the upright will be blessed.
I will give them one heart and one way, so that they will always fear Me for their own good and for the good of their children after them.
This promise belongs to you and your children and to all who are far off—to all whom the Lord our God will call to Himself.”
The one who sows to please his flesh, from the flesh will reap destruction; but the one who sows to please the Spirit, from the Spirit will reap eternal life.
Let us not grow weary in well-doing, for in due time we will reap a harvest if we do not give up.
Everyone who is proud in heart is detestable to the LORD; be assured that he will not go unpunished.
They are ever generous and quick to lend, and their children are a blessing.
Blessed are the merciful, for they will be shown mercy.
Kindness to the poor is a loan to the LORD, and He will repay the lender.
Remember this: Whoever sows sparingly will also reap sparingly, and whoever sows generously will also reap generously.
As it is written: “He has scattered abroad His gifts to the poor; His righteousness endures forever.”
Give, and it will be given to you. A good measure, pressed down, shaken together, and running over will be poured into your lap. For with the measure you use, it will be measured back to you.”
Isnʼt it to share your bread with the hungry, to bring the poor and homeless into your home, to clothe the naked when you see him, and not to turn away from your own flesh and blood?
The LORD will always guide you; He will satisfy you in a sun-scorched land and strengthen your frame. You will be like a well-watered garden, like a spring whose waters never fail.
Give generously to him, and do not let your heart be grieved when you do so. And because of this the LORD your God will bless you in all your work and in everything to which you put your hand.
Then the wise will shine like the brightness of the heavens, and those who lead many to righteousness will shine like the stars forever and ever.
consider this: Whoever turns a sinner from the error of his way will save his soul from death and cover over a multitude of sins.
Instruct those who are rich in the present age not to be conceited and not to put their hope in the uncertainty of wealth, but in God, who richly provides all things for us to enjoy.
He has dug a hole and hollowed it out; he has fallen into a pit of his own making.
His trouble recoils on himself, and his violence falls on his own head.

He is like a tree planted by the waters that sends out its roots toward the stream. It does not fear when the heat comes, and its leaves are always green. It does not worry in a year of drought, nor does it cease to produce fruit.
Though I am free of obligation to anyone, I make myself a slave to everyone, to win as many as possible.
I do all this for the sake of the gospel, so that I may share in its blessings.
